For the Liouville function on every fixed pair of nonproportional affine forms, the correlation sum up to $X$ is $O(X/(\log X)^c)$ for an absolute $c>0$, with the implied constant depending on the forms.” “For two one-bounded multiplicative functions, if at least one is uniformly nonpretentious against all Dirichlet-character twists with frequency $|t|\le N$, then their shifted and nonproportional affine correlation sums divided by $N$ tend to zero. These are ordinary averages, with no logarithmic averaging.” Quoted, not judged: AMVO has not compared this Lean statement with the family's claims or with the manuscripts.
exact_statement:
theorem binary_corrected_elliott
    (f₁ f₂ : ℕ → ℂ) (hf₁ : OneBounded f₁) (hf₂ : OneBounded f₂)
    (hm₁ : Multiplicative f₁) (hm₂ : Multiplicative f₂)
    (hNP : UniformlyNonpretentious f₁ ∨ UniformlyNonpretentious f₂)
    (h₁ h₂ : ℕ) (hne : h₁ ≠ h₂) :
    Tendsto (shiftAverage f₁ f₂ h₁ h₂) atTop (nhds 0)
